title: Crawler Dozer with Ripper (~70 t class)
model_title: Crawler Dozer with Semi-U Blade and Single-Shank Ripper (~70 t class)

introduction.definition: The ~70 t crawler dozer prepares the ground for mining and restores it afterwards. It clears vegetation, strips the topsoil (seed bank) separately from the overburden, rips the softer parts of the ferricrete caprock and the friable ore where blasting is not needed, builds ROM-pad stockpiles and haul-road berms, and reshapes mined-out pits for rehabilitation. The semi-U blade pushes; the parallelogram single-shank ripper breaks hard ground.
applications: Clearing and topsoil stripping ahead of mining (topsoil kept separate for rehabilitation)
Ripping caprock/hard ore instead of drilling and blasting where possible
ROM-pad stockpile building, berms, road edges and drainage
Final landform shaping; rehabilitation deep ripping on the contour to 1–2 m with a deep-ripping or winged-tine ripper (one unit of the fleet)
key_points: Single-shank parallelogram ripper, max penetration ≈ 1.5 m (standard shank); ≈ 1–1.5 m in production ripping
Parallelogram linkage keeps the ripper tip angle constant as it goes down
Rip in first gear; doze downhill and in slots (or blade-to-blade) to reduce spillage
Never turn or reverse with the ripper in the ground

steps.text: The diesel drives the tracks through a torque converter, a powershift transmission, the steering system and double-reduction final drives.
The lift cylinders lower the blade; the push arms pivot on trunnions on the track frames and the cutting edge enters the ground.
Material rolls up the concave mouldboard and forms a load in front of the blade; the semi-U wings keep it from spilling.
At the end of the push the operator lifts the blade and reverses for the next pass.

For hard ground: lower the tip onto the ground and move off slowly in first gear while lowering the ripper; the tip pulls itself in to about 1–1.5 m and the shank cracks the layer as the dozer moves forward. Raise the shank before stopping, turning or reversing.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Dozing production falls steeply with push distance: best below ~30–60 m; slot dozing and downhill pushing raise production by roughly 20–30 % (rule of thumb).

items.problem: Bent/broken shank or cracked ripper frame
causes: Turning or reversing with the shank in the ground
Ripping too deep in hard ferricrete
remedies: Raise the shank before steering or reversing; match depth to the material
Clean belly pans daily; fix leaks; fire suppression
Measure and plan rebuilds; limit high-speed reverse

safety: Edge (berm) awareness when pushing over a tip; never push with the tracks hanging over an edge.
Visibility around the blade and ripper; positive communication with light vehicles and spotters.
Clean debris from the engine bay to prevent fires; fire suppression fitted.

Before leaving the cab or working near the machine: blade and ripper on the ground, parking brake on, implement lock engaged, engine off, LOTO; never work under a raised blade or ripper unless it is mechanically blocked.
Clearing: keep the FOPS cab doors and windows closed; push trees over with the blade raised high on the trunk; watch for falling limbs and spring-back.
Three points of contact on the access steps.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Crawler Dozer with Ripper (~70 t class).
Walk-around: cutting edges, end bits, ripper tip, track sag/tension, leaks, guards; drain the fuel water separator; check the air-filter restriction indicator.
Clean radiator and belly guards of debris (vegetation is a fire risk).
Oil samples (engine, hydraulic, transmission, final drives) 250 h; engine oil & filter change 500 h; transmission/final-drive oil ≈ 2,000 h; hydraulic oil ≈ 4,000 h or by oil analysis.
Undercarriage measurement.
Planned component change-out (engine, transmission, final drives).
Undercarriage rebuild by measured wear.
Watch for ripper tip or shank-protector loss: missing tip. Common cause: worn retainer pin.
Watch for bent/broken shank or cracked ripper frame: shank out of line. Common cause: turning or reversing with the shank in the ground.
Watch for fire in the engine bay: smoke, alarm. Common cause: debris build-up from clearing vegetation.
Record every inspection so trends — wear, temperatures, pressures, leaks and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: Why is topsoil stripped and stored separately?
options: It holds the seed bank and soil life needed for rehabilitation
questions.explanation: Topsoil is returned to rehabilitate mined land.

questions.question: What does the parallelogram linkage do for the ripper?
options: Keeps the shank/tip angle constant as it is lowered
questions.explanation: Constant tip angle gives good penetration at all depths.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of ripping instead of drilling and blasting?
options: Lower cost and no explosives where the ground is rippable
questions.explanation: Rippable ground avoids blasting cost and hazards.

questions.question: Dozing production is best when…
options: Push distances are short and downhill, ideally in slots
questions.explanation: Short downhill pushes in slots are most productive.

questions.question: What pivots the blade push arms?
options: Trunnions on the track roller frames
questions.explanation: Push arms pin to trunnions on the track frames.

questions.question: In which gear should you rip?
questions.explanation: Ripping needs maximum drawbar pull at low speed.

questions.question: What must you do before turning or reversing while ripping?
options: Raise the shank fully out of the ground
questions.explanation: Turning or reversing with the shank in the ground bends shanks and cracks the ripper frame.

controls: Steering/direction joystick (left) with gear up/down and auto-shift buttons, blade joystick (right: raise/lower, tilt), ripper lever, decelerator pedal, service brake pedal, parking brake, engine-speed dial, implement lock lever
pre_start: Walk-around, debris removal from belly pans, fluid levels, track tension, cutting edges and ripper tip
start_up: Seat belt on, transmission in neutral, parking brake and implement lock on, then start (neutral-start interlock)
Warm up, check gauges, release the implement lock, test blade, ripper, brakes and steering
Sound the horn and confirm the area is clear (spotter or proximity system) before moving
normal: Strip topsoil in a separate pass to its own stockpile or straight to rehabilitation
Rip in first gear in straight passes; if the tracks start to slip, raise the shank slightly to reduce depth — never spin the tracks
Never turn or reverse with the ripper in the ground — raise the shank fully before steering or backing up
Doze downhill in slots; keep push distances short
shut_down: Stop on level ground away from edges and drains; neutral and parking brake on; lower blade and ripper flat to the ground; engage the implement lock
Idle 3–5 min to cool the turbo; engine off, key and master switch off; exit facing the machine with three points of contact
alarms_interlocks: Neutral-start interlock; implement (hydraulic) lockout; seat-belt / park-brake interlock
Reversing alarm; proximity detection / collision avoidance
Engine and hydraulic temperature; low engine-oil pressure; coolant level; air-filter restriction
tips: Keep a full blade but do not stall the tracks
Leave the ground graded for trucks and drainage
